lesson.subtitle: Lesson 2 -- The Clause That Was Never There
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Samuel Rodrigues | Lesson 2 -- Taking Control of the Room

listenings.text: Samuel, it's Paulo at Verde Energia. I've just come out of the board meeting and I need to be straight with you. The board is asking why we signed that supply contract without a force majeure provision. When the regulator suspended the licence, we had no way to seek a remedy, and the whole deal fell through. Nobody is blaming you personally, but they want a note by Monday explaining what happened and what we do differently next time. I said you would look into it. Call me when you have read the file.

Samuel, Diane here. I read your note on the Verde matter and I want to give you one piece of advice before Monday. Do not write it as an apology. Write it as an analysis. If the provision had been in the contract, the company would have had a remedy, and that sentence alone tells the board you understand the risk. Then say what you will require in every future contract: a force majeure provision, a clear termination clause, and a cap on liability. Boards do not want regret. They want the next decision.

items.situation: The board asks what went wrong. Answer in one sentence, using the third conditional.
tips: If the provision had been in the contract, we would have had a remedy.
Had that clause been included, the termination notice would not have been valid.

items.situation: A partner asks whether the outcome was avoidable. Say it was, without blaming a colleague.
tips: With the benefit of hindsight, the provision should have stayed in.
The risk might have been covered if we had kept the original wording.

items.situation: The client asks what you will require in every future contract of this kind.
tips: I would require a force majeure provision and a cap on liability.
We will not sign without a clear termination clause.

items.situation: The counterparty says the deal fell through because of your client. Push back, politely.
tips: I see it differently. The suspension was an act of a public authority.
That is one reading, but the contract is silent on that point.

items.situation: Close the meeting by saying what happens next and by when.
tips: I will look into the file and come back to you by Monday.
We will come up with revised wording before the next round.
